How well does the 700 kWh block threshold in Eversource's proposed Rate 6 match
actual pre-heat-pump monthly electricity use? Rate 6 assumes that all homes consume
roughly 700 kWh per month during the winter heating season (November–March), and
charges a lower Block 2 rate only on kWh above that threshold. If a home's baseline
usage is well below 700, the discount never kicks in — even after a heat pump is
installed, most of the incremental load lands in Block 1 at the full rate. If a home's
baseline usage is well above 700, the discount applies to kWh that are not actually
incremental heat pump load.

This notebook visualizes the distribution of pre-heat-pump monthly electricity
consumption during winter months across CT Eversource homes to assess how
representative the 700 kWh threshold is.

```{python}
SEG_DEFAULT_CALIBRATED = segment_name(DEFAULT_SCENARIO, "calibrated")

THRESHOLD_KWH = 700.0

# Rate 6 block rates (from ct_eversource_rate6 tariff JSON)
BLOCK1_RATE = 0.13570  # $/kWh — delivery volumetric, all kWh up to 700 in winter
BLOCK2_RATE = 0.11656  # $/kWh — delivery volumetric, kWh above 700 in winter
BLOCK_DISCOUNT = BLOCK1_RATE - BLOCK2_RATE  # intended discount per HP kWh

N_BANDS = 50  # percentile bands for ribbon charts

print(f"winter_months={WINTER_MONTHS} → {WINTER_MONTH_LABELS}")
```

## Load pre-heat-pump monthly electricity

We load monthly `elec_grid_kwh` from the upgrade-0 (pre-heat-pump) precalc segment,
restricted to Eversource buildings and winter months only. This is the consumption
that Rate 6's 700 kWh block threshold is meant to approximate.

```{python}
#| label: load-monthly-kwh

monthly_winter = (
    load_master_bills(STATE, BATCH, SEG_DEFAULT_PRECALC)
    .filter(
        (pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == UTILITY)

        "weight",
        "month",

)

    monthly_winter, code_col="postprocess_group.heating_type_v2"

print(f"{monthly_winter.height:,} building-months")
print(f"{monthly_winter['bldg_id'].n_unique():,} unique buildings")
monthly_winter.head(10)
```

## Dispersion statistics

Before plotting, let's compute the weighted mean, median, standard deviation,
and key percentiles of monthly winter kWh across all fossil-fuel-heated homes.

```{python}
#| label: dispersion-stats

def weighted_stats(df: pl.DataFrame, col: str = "monthly_kwh") -> dict:
    """Compute weighted summary statistics for a column."""
    w = df["weight"]
    x = df[col]
    total_w = w.sum()
    w_mean = float((x * w).sum() / total_w)
    w_var = float(((x - w_mean) ** 2 * w).sum() / total_w)
    w_std = w_var**0.5
    w_median = weighted_quantile(df.select(pl.col(col), "weight"), col, 0.5)
    w_p10 = weighted_quantile(df.select(pl.col(col), "weight"), col, 0.10)
    w_p25 = weighted_quantile(df.select(pl.col(col), "weight"), col, 0.25)
    w_p75 = weighted_quantile(df.select(pl.col(col), "weight"), col, 0.75)
    w_p90 = weighted_quantile(df.select(pl.col(col), "weight"), col, 0.90)
    pct_below = float((df.filter(pl.col(col) < THRESHOLD_KWH)["weight"].sum()) / total_w)
    pct_above = float((df.filter(pl.col(col) >= THRESHOLD_KWH)["weight"].sum()) / total_w)
    return {
        "mean": w_mean,
        "median": w_median,
        "std": w_std,
        "p10": w_p10,
        "p25": w_p25,
        "p75": w_p75,
        "p90": w_p90,
        "pct_below_threshold": pct_below,
        "pct_above_threshold": pct_above,
        "cv": w_std / w_mean if w_mean else 0,
    }


stats_all = weighted_stats(monthly_fossil)
stats_natgas = weighted_stats(monthly_fossil.filter(pl.col("fuel_group") == "Natural gas"))
stats_delivered = weighted_stats(monthly_fossil.filter(pl.col("fuel_group") == "Oil/propane"))

for label, s in [("All fossil", stats_all), ("Natural gas", stats_natgas), ("Oil/propane", stats_delivered)]:
    print(f"\n--- {label} ---")
    print(f"  Mean:   {s['mean']:,.0f} kWh")
    print(f"  Median: {s['median']:,.0f} kWh")
    print(f"  Std:    {s['std']:,.0f} kWh")
    print(f"  CV:     {s['cv']:.2f}")
    print(f"  P10:    {s['p10']:,.0f} kWh")
    print(f"  P25:    {s['p25']:,.0f} kWh")
    print(f"  P75:    {s['p75']:,.0f} kWh")
    print(f"  P90:    {s['p90']:,.0f} kWh")
    print(f"  Below {THRESHOLD_KWH:.0f} kWh: {s['pct_below_threshold']:.1%}")
    print(f"  At or above {THRESHOLD_KWH:.0f} kWh: {s['pct_above_threshold']:.1%}")
```

## Histogram: all fossil-heated homes

The histogram shows the distribution of monthly electricity consumption during winter
months (November–March) for all fossil-fuel-heated CT Eversource homes, *before*
switching to a heat pump. The vertical dashed line at 700 kWh marks Rate 6's block
threshold — everything to the left is billed at the full Block 1 rate under Rate 6.

```{python}
#| label: fig-winter-kwh-hist-all
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of pre-heat-pump monthly electricity consumption during winter months (November–March) for all fossil-fuel-heated CT Eversource homes. Dashed line at 700 kWh marks Rate 6's block threshold."

_xlim_lo = weighted_quantile(monthly_fossil.select("monthly_kwh", "weight"), "monthly_kwh", 0.005)
_xlim_hi = weighted_quantile(monthly_fossil.select("monthly_kwh", "weight"), "monthly_kwh", 0.995)

_mean_all = stats_all["mean"]

p = (
    plt.ggplot(monthly_fossil, plt.aes(x="monthly_kwh", weight="weight"))
    + plt.geom_histogram(binwidth=50, fill=SB_COLORS["sky"], color="white", alpha=0.85)
    + plt.geom_vline(xintercept=THRESHOLD_KWH, linetype="dashed", color=SB_COLORS["carrot"], size=1)
    + plt.annotate(
        "text",
        x=THRESHOLD_KWH + 20,
        y=float("inf"),
        label=f"{THRESHOLD_KWH:.0f} kWh",
        va="top",
        ha="left",
        color=SB_COLORS["carrot"],
        size=11,
        fontweight="bold",
    )
    + plt.geom_vline(xintercept=_mean_all, linetype="solid", color=SB_COLORS["midnight"], size=0.8)
    + plt.annotate(
        "text",
        x=_mean_all - 20,
        y=float("inf"),
        label=f"Mean: {_mean_all:,.0f} kWh",
        va="top",
        ha="right",
        color=SB_COLORS["midnight"],
        size=11,
        fontweight="bold",
    )
    + plt.scale_x_continuous(
        labels=lambda vals: [f"{v:,.0f}" for v in vals],
    )
    + plt.scale_y_continuous(
        labels=lambda vals: [f"{v:,.0f}" for v in vals],
    )
    + plt.coord_cartesian(xlim=(_xlim_lo, _xlim_hi))
    + plt.labs(
        x="Monthly electricity (kWh)",

        title="Pre-heat-pump winter electricity use vs. Rate 6's 700 kWh threshold",
        subtitle=f"Fossil-fuel-heated homes, Nov–Mar · Mean: {stats_all['mean']:,.0f} kWh · Median: {stats_all['median']:,.0f} kWh · {stats_all['pct_below_threshold']:.0%} below threshold",
    )
    + theme_switchbox()
```

## Load post-heat-pump monthly electricity

To build ribbon charts showing how the 700 kWh threshold classifies each home's
load, we need both pre-HP and post-HP monthly kWh. The post-HP data comes from the
calibrated segment (upgrade 2 = heat pump retrofit).

```{python}
#| label: load-post-hp-kwh

monthly_post = (
    load_master_bills(STATE, BATCH, SEG_DEFAULT_CALIBRATED)
    .filter(
        (pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == UTILITY)
        & (pl.col("upgrade") == 2)
        & (pl.col("month").is_in(WINTER_MONTH_LABELS))
    )
    .select(
        "bldg_id",
        "month",
        pl.col("elec_grid_kwh").alias("post_kwh"),
    )
    .collect()
)

print(f"{monthly_post.height:,} post-HP building-months")
print(f"{monthly_post['bldg_id'].n_unique():,} unique buildings")
```

Join pre-HP and post-HP monthly kWh, keeping only fossil-fuel-heated homes. Then
compute per-building winter averages and threshold classification metrics.

```{python}
#| label: build-bldg-threshold

monthly_joined = (
    monthly_fossil.join(monthly_post, on=["bldg_id", "month"], how="inner")
    .with_columns(
        (pl.col("post_kwh") - pl.col("monthly_kwh")).clip(lower_bound=0).alias("incr_kwh"),
        pl.when(pl.col("post_kwh") > THRESHOLD_KWH)
        .then(
            pl.col("post_kwh")
            - pl.max_horizontal("monthly_kwh", pl.lit(THRESHOLD_KWH))
        )
        .otherwise(0.0)
        .alias("hp_b2"),
        pl.when(pl.col("monthly_kwh") > THRESHOLD_KWH)
        .then(pl.col("monthly_kwh") - THRESHOLD_KWH)
        .otherwise(0.0)
        .alias("base_b2"),
    )
)

bldg_threshold = (
    monthly_joined.group_by(
        "bldg_id", "weight", "postprocess_group.heating_type_v2", "fuel_group"
    )
    .agg(
        pl.col("monthly_kwh").mean().alias("avg_pre"),
        pl.col("post_kwh").mean().alias("avg_post"),
        pl.col("incr_kwh").mean().alias("avg_incr"),
        pl.col("hp_b2").mean().alias("avg_hp_b2"),
        pl.col("base_b2").mean().alias("avg_base_b2"),
    )
    .filter(pl.col("avg_post") > pl.col("avg_pre"))
    .with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("avg_incr") > 0)
        .then((pl.col("avg_hp_b2") / pl.col("avg_incr")).clip(0, 1))
        .otherwise(1.0)
        .alias("capture_rate"),
        pl.when(pl.col("avg_pre") > 0)
        .then((pl.col("avg_base_b2") / pl.col("avg_pre")).clip(0, 1))
        .otherwise(0.0)
        .alias("windfall_rate"),
    )
)

print(f"{bldg_threshold.height:,} buildings with threshold metrics")
bldg_threshold.head(5)
```

Filter to delivered-fuel homes only (Rate 6's target population) and load income
data for the regressivity analysis.

```{python}
#| label: df-income

bldg_df = bldg_threshold.filter(pl.col("fuel_group") == "Oil/propane")

income_col = (
    load_master_bills(STATE, BATCH, SEG_DEFAULT_PRECALC)
    .filter(
        (pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == UTILITY)
        & (pl.col("upgrade") == 0)
        & (pl.col("month") == "Annual")
    )
    .select("bldg_id", "in.representative_income")
    .collect()
)

bldg_df = bldg_df.join(income_col, on="bldg_id", how="left")

# Weighted income terciles
_sorted = bldg_df.sort("in.representative_income")
_cum_w = _sorted["weight"].cum_sum()
_total_w = _sorted["weight"].sum()
_sorted = _sorted.with_columns(
    pl.when(_cum_w / _total_w <= 1 / 3)
    .then(pl.lit("Low income"))
    .when(_cum_w / _total_w <= 2 / 3)
    .then(pl.lit("Middle income"))
    .otherwise(pl.lit("High income"))
    .alias("income_tercile")
)
bldg_df = _sorted

# Tercile income breakpoints
_low = bldg_df.filter(pl.col("income_tercile") == "Low income")
_mid = bldg_df.filter(pl.col("income_tercile") == "Middle income")
_hi = bldg_df.filter(pl.col("income_tercile") == "High income")
_break_low_mid = float(_low["in.representative_income"].max())
_break_mid_high = float(_mid["in.representative_income"].max())

print(f"Delivered-fuel homes: {bldg_df.height:,}")
print(f"Income tercile breaks: ${_break_low_mid:,.0f} / ${_break_mid_high:,.0f}")
for t in ["Low income", "Middle income", "High income"]:
    sub = bldg_df.filter(pl.col("income_tercile") == t)
    sw = sub["weight"].sum()
    med_inc = weighted_quantile(
        sub.select(pl.col("in.representative_income").alias("v"), "weight"), "v", 0.5
    )
    print(f"  {t}: {sub.height} bldgs, median income ${med_inc:,.0f}")
```

## Ribbon chart helper

The ribbon chart ranks homes by pre-HP winter electricity on the x-axis, then shows
pre-HP and post-HP consumption as lines. Three colored regions classify how the 700
kWh threshold interacts with each home's load:

- **Sky blue**: Incremental HP load correctly in Block 2 (discounted)
- **Carrot orange**: Incremental HP load trapped in Block 1 (full rate)
- **Saffron yellow**: Pre-existing base load in Block 2 (windfall discount)

```{python}
#| label: ribbon-helper

def make_ribbon(
    ax: matplotlib.axes.Axes,
    sub: pl.DataFrame,
    threshold: float,
    title: str,
    *,
    subtitle: str | None = None,
    show_legend: bool = False,
    show_post: bool = True,
    y_max_override: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Draw a ribbon chart on the given axes."""
    sub = sub.sort("avg_pre").with_columns(
        (pl.col("weight").cum_sum() / pl.col("weight").sum() * 100).alias("pctile"),
        (
            (pl.col("weight").cum_sum() / pl.col("weight").sum() * N_BANDS)
            .floor()
            .clip(upper_bound=N_BANDS - 1)
        )
        .cast(pl.Int32)
        .alias("band"),
    )
    bands = (
        sub.group_by("band")
        .agg(
            (pl.col("pctile") * pl.col("weight")).sum() / pl.col("weight").sum(),
            (pl.col("avg_pre") * pl.col("weight")).sum() / pl.col("weight").sum(),
            (pl.col("avg_post") * pl.col("weight")).sum() / pl.col("weight").sum(),
        )
        .sort("band")
    )

    x = bands["pctile"].to_numpy()
    pre_y = bands["avg_pre"].to_numpy()
    post_y = bands["avg_post"].to_numpy()
    thr = np.full_like(x, threshold)

    if show_post:
        ax.fill_between(
            x,
            np.maximum(pre_y, thr),
            np.maximum(post_y, thr),
            where=(np.maximum(post_y, thr) > np.maximum(pre_y, thr)),
            color=SB_COLORS["sky"],
            alpha=0.45,
            label="HP load in Block 2 (discounted)" if show_legend else None,
            linewidth=0,
        )
        ax.fill_between(
            x,
            pre_y,
            np.minimum(post_y, thr),
            where=(pre_y < thr) & (np.minimum(post_y, thr) > pre_y),
            color=SB_COLORS["carrot"],
            alpha=0.55,
            label="HP load in Block 1 (full rate)" if show_legend else None,
            linewidth=0,
        )
        ax.fill_between(
            x,
            thr,
            pre_y,
            where=(pre_y > thr),
            color=SB_COLORS["saffron"],
            alpha=0.45,
            label="Base load in Block 2 (windfall)" if show_legend else None,
            linewidth=0,
        )
        ax.plot(
            x, post_y, color="#2196F3", linewidth=2,
            label="Post-HP consumption" if show_legend else None, zorder=5,
        )

    ax.plot(
        x, pre_y, color=SB_COLORS["midnight"], linewidth=2,
        label="Pre-HP consumption" if show_legend else None, zorder=5,
    )
    ax.axhline(
        y=threshold, color=SB_COLORS["carrot"], linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5, zorder=4,
    )
    ax.annotate(
        f"{threshold:.0f} kWh",
        xy=(1, threshold + 25),
        fontsize=10,
        fontweight="bold",
        color=SB_COLORS["carrot"],
    )

    if y_max_override is not None:
        y_max = y_max_override
    elif show_post:
        y_max = max(post_y) * 1.08
    else:
        y_max = max(pre_y) * 1.15
    ax.set_xlim(0, 100)
    ax.set_ylim(0, y_max)
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(ticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:,.0f}"))
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", pad=6)
    ax.set_ylabel("Avg monthly kWh", fontsize=11)

    if subtitle:
        ax.annotate(
            subtitle,
            xy=(50, y_max * 0.92),
            fontsize=10,
            ha="center",
            fontstyle="italic",
            color="#555555",
        )
    if show_legend:
        ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=9, framealpha=0.9)
```

## Incidence and severity statistics

How many delivered-fuel homes are affected by each classification error, and how
severe is the misclassification for the typical affected home?

```{python}
#| label: incidence-severity

def incidence_severity(
    df: pl.DataFrame,
) -> dict:
    """Compute incidence and severity of threshold misclassification."""
    sw = df["weight"].sum()

    has_orange = df.filter(pl.col("capture_rate") < 1.0)
    has_yellow = df.filter(pl.col("windfall_rate") > 0)

    pct_any_orange = float(has_orange["weight"].sum() / sw)
    pct_any_yellow = float(has_yellow["weight"].sum() / sw)

    orange_kwh = has_orange.with_columns(
        (pl.col("avg_incr") - pl.col("avg_hp_b2")).alias("trapped_kwh")
    )
    med_trapped = (
        weighted_quantile(
            orange_kwh.select(pl.col("trapped_kwh").alias("v"), "weight"), "v", 0.5
        )
        if has_orange.height > 0
        else 0.0
    )
    med_windfall = (
        weighted_quantile(
            has_yellow.select(pl.col("avg_base_b2").alias("v"), "weight"), "v", 0.5
        )
        if has_yellow.height > 0
        else 0.0
    )

    mean_capture = float((df["capture_rate"] * df["weight"]).sum() / sw)

    return {
        "pct_any_orange": pct_any_orange,
        "pct_any_yellow": pct_any_yellow,
        "median_trapped_kwh": med_trapped,
        "median_windfall_kwh": med_windfall,
        "mean_capture": mean_capture,
    }


is_all = incidence_severity(bldg_df)

print("=== All delivered-fuel homes ===")
print(f"  % with any HP load trapped (orange):  {is_all['pct_any_orange']:.1%}")
print(f"  % with any base-load windfall (yellow): {is_all['pct_any_yellow']:.1%}")
print(f"  Median trapped kWh/mo (if affected):  {is_all['median_trapped_kwh']:,.0f}")
print(f"  Median windfall kWh/mo (if affected): {is_all['median_windfall_kwh']:,.0f}")
print(f"  Mean capture rate: {is_all['mean_capture']:.1%}")
```

## Effective discount and regressivity metrics

For each home, the effective rate on incremental HP load is a weighted average of
Block 1 and Block 2 rates, depending on how much HP load lands in each block. The
percent of the intended discount received is then
`(Block1 - effective_rate) / (Block1 - Block2)`.

```{python}
#| label: effective-discount

def _effective_discount_pct(df: pl.DataFrame) -> float:
    """Weighted mean percent of intended discount received."""
    sw = df["weight"].sum()
    df2 = df.with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("avg_incr") > 0)
        .then(
            (
                (pl.col("avg_incr") - pl.col("avg_hp_b2")) * BLOCK1_RATE
                + pl.col("avg_hp_b2") * BLOCK2_RATE
            )
            / pl.col("avg_incr")
        )
        .otherwise(BLOCK1_RATE)
        .alias("eff_rate"),
    )
    mean_eff = float((df2["eff_rate"] * df2["weight"]).sum() / sw)
    return (BLOCK1_RATE - mean_eff) / BLOCK_DISCOUNT


# Income–base-load correlation
def _weighted_corr(df: pl.DataFrame, col_x: str, col_y: str) -> float:
    x = df[col_x].to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df[col_y].to_numpy().astype(float)
    w = df["weight"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    mask = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    x, y, w = x[mask], y[mask], w[mask]
    sw = w.sum()
    mx = (x * w).sum() / sw
    my = (y * w).sum() / sw
    cov_xy = (w * (x - mx) * (y - my)).sum() / sw
    sx = np.sqrt((w * (x - mx) ** 2).sum() / sw)
    sy = np.sqrt((w * (y - my) ** 2).sum() / sw)
    return float(cov_xy / (sx * sy)) if sx > 0 and sy > 0 else 0.0


income_base_corr = _weighted_corr(bldg_df, "in.representative_income", "avg_pre")
print(f"Income–base-load correlation (DF): {income_base_corr:.3f}")

print(f"\nBlock 1 rate: {BLOCK1_RATE * 100:.3f} ¢/kWh")
print(f"Block 2 rate: {BLOCK2_RATE * 100:.3f} ¢/kWh")
print(f"Intended discount: {BLOCK_DISCOUNT * 100:.3f} ¢/kWh")
print()

for tercile in ["Low income", "Middle income", "High income"]:
    sub = bldg_df.filter(pl.col("income_tercile") == tercile)
    pct = _effective_discount_pct(sub)
    _is = incidence_severity(sub)
    print(
        f"{tercile}: {pct:.0%} of discount received, "
        f"{_is['pct_any_orange']:.0%} with trapped HP, "
        f"{_is['pct_any_yellow']:.0%} with windfall"
    )
```

```{python}
#| label: export-report-vars

report_vars: dict = {}

    report_vars[f"winter_kwh_p90_{label}"] = s["p90"]
    report_vars[f"winter_kwh_pct_below_{label}"] = s["pct_below_threshold"]
    report_vars[f"winter_kwh_pct_above_{label}"] = s["pct_above_threshold"]

# Threshold proximity stats (delivered-fuel, per-building avg)
_df_dists = bldg_df.with_columns(
    (pl.col("avg_pre") - THRESHOLD_KWH).abs().alias("dist_from_threshold")
)
_df_total_w = bldg_df["weight"].sum()
report_vars["pct_within_50_of_threshold_df"] = float(
    bldg_df.filter(
        (pl.col("avg_pre") >= THRESHOLD_KWH - 50)
        & (pl.col("avg_pre") <= THRESHOLD_KWH + 50)
    )["weight"].sum()
    / _df_total_w
)
report_vars["median_dist_from_threshold_df"] = weighted_quantile(
    _df_dists.select(pl.col("dist_from_threshold").alias("v"), "weight"), "v", 0.5
)
_p10_df = weighted_quantile(
    bldg_df.select(pl.col("avg_pre").alias("v"), "weight"), "v", 0.10
)
_p90_df = weighted_quantile(
    bldg_df.select(pl.col("avg_pre").alias("v"), "weight"), "v", 0.90
)
report_vars["winter_kwh_p10_delivered_bldg"] = _p10_df
report_vars["winter_kwh_p90_delivered_bldg"] = _p90_df

# Block rate values
report_vars["block1_rate_cents"] = BLOCK1_RATE * 100
report_vars["block2_rate_cents"] = BLOCK2_RATE * 100
report_vars["block_discount_cents"] = BLOCK_DISCOUNT * 100

# Incidence and severity (all DF)
report_vars["pct_any_orange_df"] = is_all["pct_any_orange"]
report_vars["pct_any_yellow_df"] = is_all["pct_any_yellow"]
report_vars["median_trapped_kwh_df"] = is_all["median_trapped_kwh"]
report_vars["median_windfall_kwh_df"] = is_all["median_windfall_kwh"]
report_vars["mean_capture_df"] = is_all["mean_capture"]

# Income–base-load correlation
report_vars["income_base_load_corr_df"] = income_base_corr

# Income tercile breakpoints
report_vars["income_tercile_break_low_mid"] = _break_low_mid
report_vars["income_tercile_break_mid_high"] = _break_mid_high

# Per-tercile stats
for tercile, key in [
    ("Low income", "low"),
    ("Middle income", "mid"),
    ("High income", "high"),
]:
    sub = bldg_df.filter(pl.col("income_tercile") == tercile)
    _is_t = incidence_severity(sub)
    report_vars[f"pct_discount_df_{key}"] = _effective_discount_pct(sub)
    _sw_t = sub["weight"].sum()
    _tbr = sub.with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("avg_incr") > 0)
        .then((pl.col("avg_hp_b2") + pl.col("avg_base_b2")) / pl.col("avg_incr"))
        .otherwise(0.0)
        .alias("tbr"),
    )
    report_vars[f"total_benefit_ratio_df_{key}"] = float(
        (_tbr["tbr"] * _tbr["weight"]).sum() / _sw_t
    )
    report_vars[f"pct_any_orange_df_{key}"] = _is_t["pct_any_orange"]
    report_vars[f"pct_any_yellow_df_{key}"] = _is_t["pct_any_yellow"]
    report_vars[f"median_trapped_kwh_df_{key}"] = _is_t["median_trapped_kwh"]
    report_vars[f"median_windfall_kwh_df_{key}"] = _is_t["median_windfall_kwh"]
    _med_inc = weighted_quantile(
        sub.select(pl.col("in.representative_income").alias("v"), "weight"), "v", 0.5
    )
    report_vars[f"median_income_df_{key}"] = _med_inc
    report_vars[f"income_lo_df_{key}"] = float(sub["in.representative_income"].min())
    report_vars[f"income_hi_df_{key}"] = float(sub["in.representative_income"].max())

Path("../cache").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
Path("../cache/rate6_threshold_report_variables.pkl").write_bytes(
    pickle.dumps(report_vars)
)
print(f"Exported {len(report_vars)} report vars to cache/rate6_threshold_report_variables.pkl")
```
